correctness.rationale: Marking one size-s block and deleting it is a uniform (n-s,k-1) partition, so the conditional expected singleton count is F_(k-1)(n-s), giving the exact covariance. The ordered fiber-size distribution for a random uniform surjection onto b blocks has weight product_i 1/j_i!. Log-concavity of 1/j! for positive j and preservation under convolution imply the conditional single-fiber distributions are monotone-likelihood-ratio ordered as total m increases; the new largest supported j is strictly positive, hence F_b(m) strictly decreases for all m>=b. Decreasing residual n-s thus gives strict bracket increase, and the maximal-s endpoint is positive as not all partitions at n>=k+2 have k-1 singletons. Fixed-b inclusion-exclusion Stirling asymptotics F_b(m)~m*b/(b-1)*((b-1)/b)^m yield the macroscopic boundary. Independent exact Stirling covariance comparisons, sign monotonicity and (6,3,3) zero case passed. The fixed-k theorem does not follow merely from unconditioned Bell ratios.
residual_risks: Strict decrease F_b holds for b>=2 and m>=b, with b=k-1>=2; the degenerate b=1 case was deliberately excluded.
The macroscopic cutoff holds fixed k, not k proportional to n.

evidence: Arratia–DeSalvo treat n-k of order sqrt n, not fixed k, and Mutafchiev–Savov focus on the maximum multiplicity in unconditioned partitions. Conditional factorial moments are implicit in combinatorial occupancy frameworks.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The more general occupancy framework can recover moment formulas by substitution; none of the inspected statements entails the strict monotone sign pattern and fixed-k fractional boundary.

originality.rationale: Unlike the closely related published Bell-partition result, which concerns Cov(total number of blocks, X_s) in an unconditioned model and a logarithmic threshold, this claim concerns Cov(X1,X_s) at exactly k blocks and a positive-fraction threshold. General factorial moment methods imply its raw moments but not plainly the strict one-crossing inequality.
residual_risks: Timashev 2003 complete original Russian paper was inspected; its single-size factorial moment formula could imply pieces of the mixed moment by generalization, and other older conditional occupancy literature could contain the full one-switch result.
The resulting fixed-k asymptotic is not uniform when k grows.

value.rationale: The fixed-block occupancy model is fundamental in combinatorial probability; a complete covariance sign classification and a sharp linear-scale transition for singleton counts versus large blocks give a natural, reusable dependence threshold. The zero-covariance but nonindependent example clarifies the scope.
residual_risks: The conditional mixed-moment identity is classical marking; value rests on strict sign structure and fixed-k boundary, not that identity alone.

limitations: Exact sign order and asymptotic for k>=3 only, not arbitrary two non-singleton sizes.
